225	#!/usr/bin/env bash
226	# Provisions the cluster-side prerequisites for a remote build: the `build`
227	# namespace and the docker.io push secret the Job mounts. Idempotent — running
228	# it twice exits 0 and leaves exactly one namespace and one secret.
229	#
230	# Called by hand before the first `make build BUILD_TARGET=<cluster>` against a
231	# cluster. It deliberately creates no Job: jobs are per-build, rendered by
232	# hack/build-cluster.sh, which refuses to run when one already exists.
233	set -euo pipefail
234	
235	SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
236	TEMPLATE="${TEMPLATE:-${SCRIPT_DIR}/dockerconfig.json.tpl}"
237	
238	BUILD_TARGET="${1:-}"
239	NAMESPACE="${NAMESPACE:-build}"
240	BUILD_PUSH_SECRET="${BUILD_PUSH_SECRET:-buildkit-push}"
241	
242	die() {
243		echo "build-cluster-bootstrap: $*" >&2
244		exit 1
245	}
246	
247	[ -n "${BUILD_TARGET}" ] || die "usage: $(basename "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}") <sun|nukedev|nukeprod|kubectl-context>"
248	[ -f "${TEMPLATE}" ] || die "template not found: ${TEMPLATE}"
249	
250	# The same -teamvault-config value `make apply` takes (Makefile.k8s). Defaults to
251	# the config the repo's own .envrc uses, so an operator who has teamvault-cli set
252	# up does not have to export anything.
253	TEAMVAULT="${TEAMVAULT:-${HOME}/.config/teamvault-cli/config.json}"
254	[ -f "${TEAMVAULT}" ] || die "teamvault config not found: ${TEAMVAULT} (set TEAMVAULT to override)"
255	command -v teamvault-cli >/dev/null 2>&1 ||
256		die "teamvault-cli not found on PATH; it resolves the lookup key in ${TEMPLATE}"
257	
258	# Shared with hack/build-cluster.sh so the alias mapping cannot drift between
259	# provisioning and building.
260	source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/cluster-alias.sh"
261	
262	# The rendered credential lives in a 600 temp file for the length of one
263	# `create secret --dry-run` and is removed on every exit path. It is never
264	# echoed, never logged, and never written into the repo.
265	RENDERED="$(mktemp)"
266	chmod 600 "${RENDERED}"
267	trap 'rm -f "${RENDERED}"' EXIT INT TERM
268	
269	echo "build-cluster-bootstrap: cluster ${BUILD_TARGET} (kubectl context ${KUBE_CONTEXT})"
270	
271	kc create namespace "${NAMESPACE}" --dry-run=client -o yaml | kc apply -f -
272	echo "build-cluster-bootstrap: namespace ${NAMESPACE} present"
273	
274	# The lookup key comes from the template, so the template stays the single
275	# declaration of which TeamVault item and which registry this secret is for.
276	TEAMVAULT_KEY="$(sed -nE 's/.*"([A-Za-z0-9]{6,12})" \| teamvaultUser.*/\1/p' "${TEMPLATE}" | head -1)"
277	[ -n "${TEAMVAULT_KEY}" ] || die "no teamvaultUser lookup key found in ${TEMPLATE}"
278	
279	# teamvault-cli, not teamvault-config-parser: the parser takes its password from
280	# the config file, which holds only url and user, so it authenticates unprivileged
281	# and gets 403 on this item. The CLI reads the login from the macOS Keychain.
282	TV_USER="$(teamvault-cli username --teamvault-config "${TEAMVAULT}" --teamvault-key="${TEAMVAULT_KEY}")"
283	TV_PASS="$(teamvault-cli password --teamvault-config "${TEAMVAULT}" --teamvault-key="${TEAMVAULT_KEY}")"
284	[ -n "${TV_USER}" ] && [ -n "${TV_PASS}" ] || die "teamvault returned an empty credential for key ${TEAMVAULT_KEY}"
285	
286	# docker.io's canonical auths key, per the template.
287	printf '{"auths":{"https://index.docker.io/v1/":{"username":"%s","password":"%s"}}}' \
288		"${TV_USER}" "${TV_PASS}" >"${RENDERED}"
289	unset TV_USER TV_PASS
290	[ -s "${RENDERED}" ] || die "failed to render ${TEMPLATE}"
291	
292	kc create secret generic "${BUILD_PUSH_SECRET}" \
293		-n "${NAMESPACE}" \
294		--type=kubernetes.io/dockerconfigjson \
295		--from-file=.dockerconfigjson="${RENDERED}" \
296		--dry-run=client -o yaml | kc apply -f -
297	echo "build-cluster-bootstrap: secret ${NAMESPACE}/${BUILD_PUSH_SECRET} present"
298	
299	echo "build-cluster-bootstrap: ready — make build BUILD_TARGET=${BUILD_TARGET}"
300	```

145	## Security / Abuse
146	
147	- The push credential exists only as a cluster secret, mounted into the build pod. It is never written to the invoking machine, never passed as a make variable, and never printed.

150	- `buildctl-daemonless.sh` runs rootless with `--oci-worker-no-process-sandbox`. No privileged pod, no host namespace, no Docker socket.

152	- `REF` is passed as a clone argument, not interpolated into a shell string, so a crafted ref cannot execute commands in the init container.
